explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/479: 'Is it true that, for all k ≠ 1, there are infinitely many n such that 2^n ≡ k (mod n)?' The Lean statement: for every integer k ≠ 1, {n : ℕ | 2^n ≡ k [ZMOD n]} is infinite. Taking k ∈ ℤ allows negative k such as −1, consistent with the page's mention of the case k = −1. The values n = 0 (which would need k = 1) and n = 1 (always a solution) contribute at most finitely many elements, so infinitude is unaffected. Faithful (positive form of the yes/no question).
